newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and bellies end up ahead of storage data.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and bellies end up ahead of storage data.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures ended mostly higher on shortcovering and evening up ahead of the monthly USDA Cold Storage report, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.525 cent higher to 0.150 lower, with December up 0.475 at 57.975 cents a lb. Bellies ended 1.300 to 0.575 higher, with February up 1.025 at 74.975 cents.
Shortcovering developed in hogs on the back of a stronger-than-expected cash hog market Friday morning. The market appeared oversold and corrected somewhat, especially ahead of the report, they said.

Packers showed good interest for hogs despite weakness in most cash pork products and expected slow pork demand during the holiday period next week. They appear to want to boost Saturday's kill rate to make up for part of the reduced slaughter during Thanksgiving, traders added.
In hog options, locals sold calls as the time decay was large in December due to the weekend and holiday next week, pit sources said.

Bellies rallied early on local shortcovering and continued underlying support from commercials. The market appeared short-term oversold after technical selling Thursday. Fundamentals are also expected to remain strong, especially with the projections the monthly USDA Cold Storage report will show historically low frozen belly stocks, traders said.
The average analyst estimate for the report was 16.0 million lbs in cold storage on November 1. This compares with the 10-year average of 22.8 million lbs.
Even though bacon shows a seasonally weak period during the holidays, the report should lend support, they added.
However, late evening up trade pared futures from best levels, they added..
R.J. O'Brien was a notable buyer in February during the day, pit sources said.
